events.title: Emperor Kanmu moves Japan's capital to Heian-kyō
events.description: On the 22nd day of the tenth month, Emperor Kanmu formally moved his court to the new capital of Heian-kyō, modern Kyoto. It remained the imperial seat for over a thousand years; the Jidai Matsuri festival marks the date.

events.title: Peter the Great takes the title of emperor
events.description: After victory over Sweden in the Great Northern War, the Russian Senate conferred on Peter I the titles 'the Great' and Emperor of All Russia (22 October, Old Style). Russia was now formally an empire and a European great power.
events.html: After victory over Sweden in the Great Northern War, the Russian Senate conferred on Peter I the titles 'the Great' and Emperor of All Russia (22 October, Old Style). Russia was now formally an empire and a European great power.

events.title: André-Jacques Garnerin makes the first parachute descent from a balloon
events.description: Over the Parc Monceau in Paris, André-Jacques Garnerin cut his parachute free of a hydrogen balloon at about 1,000 metres. He landed safely despite violent swinging, the first frameless silk parachute jump.

events.title: Sam Houston becomes the first president of the Republic of Texas
events.description: Sam Houston, victor of San Jacinto, was inaugurated as the first elected president of the Republic of Texas at Columbia. Texas remained an independent republic until joining the United States in 1845.

events.title: Kennedy tells Americans of Soviet missiles in Cuba
events.description: In a televised address, John F. Kennedy revealed that Soviet nuclear missile sites were being built in Cuba and announced a naval 'quarantine' of the island. The crisis brought the superpowers closer to nuclear war than ever before.
